title: 朝のコーヒー
summary: A short morning routine: coffee, the weather, studying in the park, and meeting a friend.

sentences.jp: 朝{あさ}、私{わたし}はコーヒーを飲{の}みます。
sentences.en: In the morning, I drink coffee.

sentences.jp: 今日{きょう}はいい天気{てんき}です。
公園{こうえん}で日本語{にほんご}を勉強します{べんきょうします}。
sentences.en: I study Japanese at the park.

sentences.jp: それから、午後{ごご}は友達{ともだち}に会{あ}います。
sentences.en: After that, I'll meet a friend in the afternoon.

grammar.title: は — topic marker
grammar.note: 私は marks 私 as the topic (“as for me”). 午後は does the same for “the afternoon,” often with a mild contrast against the earlier part of the day. As a particle, は is pronounced わ.

grammar.title: を — object marker
grammar.note: を marks what the verb acts on: コーヒーを飲みます (drink coffee), 日本語を勉強します (study Japanese).

grammar.title: で — place of an action
grammar.note: 公園で勉強します means the studying happens at the park. Use で for where an action takes place. Use に with verbs such as 住む for where someone lives or something exists.

grammar.title: 会う takes に
grammar.note: The person you meet is marked with に, not を: 友達に会います.

grammar.title: ます — polite non-past
grammar.note: 飲みます, 勉強します, and 会います are polite non-past forms. Dictionary forms: 飲む, 勉強する, 会う. The non-past covers habits and the future, so 会います can mean “I meet” or “I will meet.”
